name: Recital 34 – 23/2
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on speeding-up environmental assessments
part_text: (34) The construction, refurbishment, operation, and decommissioning of projects can lead to incidental killing, disturbance, destruction or damage to nests and eggs of bird species protected under Directive 2009/147/EC and other species protected under Directive 92/43/EEC. The extent of killing, disturbance, destruction or damage can vary depending on the type of project and its design, the ecological importance of the area for the species and their presence in the area concerned. However, appropriate mitigation measures and use of best available technologies should be included and cumulation effects, when they are identified, taken into account, in such projects to prevent or reduce those adverse effects to insignificant levels. Best available technologies should be understood as technically recognised measures and industry best practice, based on the most recent scientific data and that are most effective, technically and economically viable as well as accessible to operators, including techniques which are proven to help avoiding occasional killing and preventing disturbance and destruction of, or damage to, nests or eggs of protected species during the construction, refurbishment, operation or decommissioning of plans.
